original_value: This paper addresses the problem of localization accuracy degradation caused by outliers of the angle of arrival (AOA). The problem of outlier detection of the AOA is converted into the detection of the estimated source position sets, which are obtained by the proposed division and greedy replacement method. The Mahalanobis distance based on robust mean and covariance matrix estimation method is then introduced to identify the outliers from the position sets. Finally, the weighted least squares method based on the reliable probabilities and distances is proposed for source localization. The simulation and experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms representative methods when unreliable AOAs are present.

result.paraphrase: This paper studies localization accuracy loss caused by angle-of-arrival (AOA) outliers. It reformulates AOA outlier detection as identifying estimated source position sets obtained through the proposed division and greedy replacement method. It then introduces a Mahalanobis-distance approach based on robust mean and covariance matrix estimation to detect outliers within the position sets. Finally, a weighted least squares method using reliable probabilities and distances is proposed for source localization. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms representative methods when unreliable AOAs are present.
